title: Morphisms of coherent formal modules whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of an ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I,\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals and $\alpha=(\alpha_n):(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde I$, $\mathcal K|_U=\widetilde K$ ($I=\mathcal I(U)$, $K=\mathcal K(U)$), let $\alpha_U:M\to N$ be the $A^\wedge$-linear map of finitely generated $A^\wedge$-modules ($A^\wedge$ the $I$-adic completion) $M=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n(U)\to N=\varprojlim_n\mathcal G_n(U)$, $\alpha_U=\varprojlim_n\alpha_n(U)$, which corresponds to $\alpha|_U$ under the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2). The following are equivalent: (1) there is $t\ge1$ such that $\mathcal K^t\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_n)=0$ and $\mathcal K^t\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha_n)=0$ for all $n\ge1$ (kernels and cokernels of $\mathcal O_X$-modules); (2) for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ there is $t\ge1$ with $K^t\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_U)=0$ and $K^t\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha_U)=0$; (3) there are a finite covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_r$ by affine opens and $t\ge1$ such that the condition of (2) holds for every $\alpha_{U_i}$; (4) there is $t\ge1$ such that the kernel and the cokernel of $\alpha$ in the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] are annihilated by $\mathcal K^t$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3). (Stacks then says that $\alpha$ is a map whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of $\mathcal K$.) Moreover, the integer $t$ of (1) may be replaced by $2t$ when passing from (3) to (1), and the commutative algebra fact behind this holds: if $0\to T\to M\xrightarrow{u}N\to Q\to0$ is an exact sequence of modules over a ring $A$ with $K^tT=K^tQ=0$, then for every ideal $J\subseteq A$ the kernel and cokernel of $u\bmod J:M/JM\to N/JN$ are annihilated by $K^{2t}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Remark 0888 (remark-inverse-systems-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-by, line 6887), conditions (1)-(3) and the commutative algebra fact of its proof, with Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine) for alpha_U; condition (4) (kernel and cokernel taken in the abelian category Coh(X, I) of Lemma 087X, lemma-inverse-systems-abelian) is added by an agent: it is how the condition is used in the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-push-pull] and [prop-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence]; its equivalence with (2) comes from the description of kernels and cokernels on affine opens in the proof of Lemma 087X

proof.text: From a uniform exponent t at every component, apply the affine-limit lemma separately on every affine U and choose the positive exponent 2t. This proves condition (1) implies (2).

Extract a finite affine subcover from quasi-compactness. Choose each local exponent, then take max(1, the supremum of the finitely many exponents). Ideal powers are antitone in the exponent, so this exponent works on the whole finite cover, including the empty-cover case. This proves (2) implies (3).

Apply the kernel and cokernel finite-cover reduction lemmas at each level, pair their conclusions, and choose exponent 2t. This proves (3) implies (1), and also proves the separate double-exponent assertion.
Use abelianness to take the canonical formal kernel fork and cokernel cofork. Apply the fixed-exponent formal affine-cover criterion to the finite covering. This proves (3) implies (4).

Apply the same fixed-exponent criterion to the covering indexed by all affine opens. Each affine has the uniform exponent of (4). This proves (4) implies (2). The five implications assemble into the four-way TFAE.
The separate commutative-algebra reduction assertion is clause (c) of the scalar quasi-inverse and reduction theorem.

lean.statement: theorem coherentFormalModule_annihilated_iff (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData) (F G : CoherentFormalModule X I) (α : F ⟶ G) : List.TFAE [(∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (kernel (α.hom.app (op n)))) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel (α.hom.app (op n))))), (∀ U : X.affineOpens, ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ K.ideal U ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) (LinearMap.ker (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)))).hom) ∧ K.ideal U ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) (↥(limit (G.obj ⋙ SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)) : ModuleCat Γ(X, U.1)) ⧸ LinearMap.range (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)))).hom)), (∃ (r : ℕ) (U : Fin r → X.affineOpens) (t : ℕ), (⨆ i, (U i).1) = ⊤ ∧ 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ i : Fin r, K.ideal (U i) ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, (U i).1) (LinearMap.ker (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op (U i).1)))).hom) ∧ K.ideal (U i) ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, (U i).1) (↥(limit (G.obj ⋙ SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op (U i).1)) : ModuleCat Γ(X, (U i).1)) ⧸ LinearMap.range (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op (U i).1)))).hom)), (∃ (k : KernelFork α) (c : CokernelCofork α), Nonempty (IsLimit k) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (k.pt.obj.obj (op n))) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (c.pt.obj.obj (op n))))]
lean.note: The affine map is the actual inverse limit of section maps, regarded over the ring of sections; the recorded affine equivalence identifies it with the restricted completed-module map. Universal kernel/cokernel forks realize condition (4) without an additional Abelian-instance hypothesis. The two companion declarations state the 2t bound and the commutative algebra clause.
